The '''Imperial Troop Transport''' ('''ITT''') was a transport model produced by [[Ubrikkian Industries]]. A [[troop transport]] like the Ubrikkian-made [[K79-S80 Imperial Troop Transport]], this version was flight-capable. It was used by the [[Galactic Empire]] and [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]'s [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]] during the [[Imperial Era|Imperial]] and [[New Republic Era]]s, and can be modified to transport [[stormtrooper]]s and heavy weaponry to battle zones<ref name="Kenobi V">{{Kenobi|Part V}}</ref> or imperial prisoners to the prison where they would serve their sentence.<ref name="Narkina 5" />

==Characteristics==	
The [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[transport]]s featured a wedge-shaped fuselage and a forward boarding ramp. It was powered by [[engine]]s and was armed with twin paired [[laser cannon]]s.<ref name="Chapter 14" /> Its interior could be modified to hold at least 36 standing stormtroopers<ref name="Kenobi V" /> or at least 20 seated prisoners.<ref name="Narkina 5" />

==History==
One Imperial transport deployed multiple [[TK stormtrooper]]s, one of which was [[Ubrik Adelhard]], the future Grand Moff and governor of the [[Anoat sector]], to put down an [[Storming of Abartolom|insurrection]] on [[Abartolom]].<ref name="Insurgency Rising 1">[[Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising 1|''Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising'' 1]]</ref>

By [[9 BBY]],<ref name="Kenobi date">{{KenobiDate|III}}</ref> some transports were stationed at the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Fortress Inquisitorius]] on [[Nur]].<ref name="Obi-Wan">{{Kenobi|Part III}}</ref> During the siege of [[Jabiim]], the Imperials deployed two such transports to besiege an anti-Imperial cell known as the [[Hidden Path]].<ref name="Kenobi V" />

[[File:Prison_barge_interior.png|thumb|left|300px|An imperial transport in prison barge configuration; the prisoners have their hands shackled in their seats]]
A modified version of the ITT,<ref name="SWE TCGSWG" /> called the [[Imperial Prison Transport]]<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion">''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''</ref>, was used in [[5 BBY]]<ref name="AndorDate">{{AndorDate|108}}</ref> to ferry prisoners from the [[Niamos Courthouse|Niamos courthouse]] to the [[prison]] where they would serve their sentence. They had caged windows and specialized seats which could be magnetized to have the prisoners' shackles attached on them, and lacked the twin laser cannons on the front. One such IPT was used to carry [[Cassian Jeron Andor]] to the [[Narkina 5 Imperial Prison Complex|Imperial Prison Complex]] on [[Narkina 5]] following his arrest on [[Niamos]].<ref name="Narkina 5" />

One was stationed aboard the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Tarkin's Will]]'', and was used by [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] [[Special Forces Trackers Unit|Pathfinder]] [[Sergeant]] [[Kes Dameron]] and his [[Marriage|wife]], the [[rebel pilot]] [[Shara Bey]], to escape the ''Tarkin's Will'' and return to the rebel [[flagship]] ''[[Home One]]'' during the [[Battle of Panisia]].<ref name="Star Wars 23" /> In [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{MandoDate|14}}.</ref> they were used by [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]'s [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]]. Two such transports participated in a [[Battle of Tython (9 ABY)|battle on Tython]] to retrieve [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] from [[Din Djarin]]. After a retreat was ordered, both ships took off in an attempt to flee. However, a [[missile]] launched from [[Boba Fett]]'s [[Z-6 jetpack]] caused one to crash into the other, destroying both.<ref name="Chapter 14" />

===Legacy===
The [[First Order]], the successor state to the Empire, employed the [[AAL-1971/9.1 Troop Transport]]s, a similar model that deployed its [[First Order stormtrooper|Stormtroopers]] to battle and maintain the state's order and peace. In addition, the [[AAL-2100/9.5 atmospheric assault lander]] was another successor utilized by the [[Final Order]].

==Behind the scenes==
The Imperial Troop Transport first appeared in the [[2020]] episode "[[Chapter 14: The Tragedy]]" of the live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''.<ref name="Chapter 14" /> ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' identifies the model as the Ubrikkian Imperial Troop Transport.<ref name="SWE TCGSWG" /> An early preview page for the [[2026]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' labeled the craft the [[Telgorn Corporation]] DX-10 transport.<ref name="Preview">{{WebCite|url=https://starwarstimeline.com/non-fiction|text=Upcoming Books and Comics: Non-Fiction|work=[https://starwarstimeline.com Once Upon a Galaxy]|archivedate=20250807163518}}</ref>
A vehicle of similar appearance was first depicted in the [[Andor Season 1|first season]] of the [[Disney+]] live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'', within the episode "[[Narkina 5 (episode)|Narkina 5]]".<ref name="Narkina 5" /> The design of the transport was confirmed to be based upon the Imperial Troop Transport<ref name="IPTDesignBasedOnITT">{{SW|url=andor-s1-e8-trivia-gallery|text=Andor | Season 1, Episode 8 - Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Image 4}}.</ref>, and the reference book [[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]], released on [[November 2]], [[2023]] in the United Kingdom, codified this through establishing it to be a repurposed version denoted as the Imperial Prison Transport.<ref name="Dawn of Rebellion" />
''
